parts: Activate sustained master research in papers/master. Use GPT-6.2 Astra/ultra as lead and GPT-6.2 Sol/ultra for bounded, versioned execution and independent checks. Read AGENTS.md, INVESTIGATION_SETUP_WORKFLOW.md, GPT_RESEARCH_MODEL_WORKFLOW.md, REFERENCE_WORKFLOW.md, the master overview, plan, sole register, ownership crosswalk and the four branch handoffs in PARALLEL_PROGRAM_20261125.md. Recompute the working manuscript and evidence revisions. Compare each new branch result with its original hypotheses and the remaining smooth types. Test direct recognition for a positive class at or below 4π² or for a hypersurface-induced class at or below 64π²/9. At immersed energy below 8π² follow a selected Morse height to its actual attaching maps. Positive subcritical entry on arbitrary smooth types remains a separate target. On the intrinsic route use one admissible physical Yamabe minimizing sequence and its actual marks, gauges and measures; seek a full separating shell, a strict same-type competitor or a proved closed rigidity or restart termination result. Coordinate with existing branch writers and freeze disjoint helper outputs. Continue through useful alternatives without routine approval, preserve scoped failures and report a verified implication with its quantifiers and remaining obstruction. Promote a result when it shortens the master proof and rebuild the PDF after manuscript changes.

I’ll check the master manuscript, register, and branch handoffs against the working tree first. Then I’ll assign disjoint checks and trace the strongest candidate implication through to its smooth conclusion.

The height analysis now recognizes a concrete class of two-handle diagrams. On the intrinsic route, a Yamabe cutoff gives a way to locate the entire outer energy mark, even when that set is disconnected. I’m checking whether two distances measured in a sufficiently wide annular chart also locate the inner mark.

The annulus check succeeded under a weaker marking hypothesis. One point of the middle sphere within \(A\rho_i\) of the quantile center suffices, provided the chart has fixed width large enough for \(A\) and the Yamabe bound. I’m also checking a replacement argument that leaves the interiors of the charged disks completely uncontrolled and charges only the collars used to remove them.

The manuscript now includes a recognition theorem for physical Yamabe metrics that are close to Einstein and nearly satisfy a spectral inequality in one Weyl block. Its threshold is non-effective. I’ve also completed the marked surgery and collar-replacement proofs and am checking the final text, references, and rebuilt PDF.

The [rebuilt 39-page master manuscript](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/output/pdf/master/chiral_weyl_energy_and_smooth_poincare.pdf) now gives a direct recognition criterion and weakens the geometric hypothesis needed for a separating cut.

**Direct recognition.** Theorem 10.3 applies to a volume-one positive Yamabe metric on any smooth homotopy four-sphere. Fix a margin below \(8\pi^2\), an \(L^p\) bound on trace-free Ricci for some \(p>2\), and \(0\le s<1\). If the \(L^2\) trace-free Ricci energy is sufficiently small and one Weyl block has sufficiently small defect
\[
\int_M\bigl(\lambda_2(W^\pm)-s\lambda_3(W^\pm)\bigr)_+^2\,dV,
\]
then the **tested metric itself** has \(E_+<4\pi^2\), so \(M\) is standard. The smallness threshold is non-effective. The proof obtains a smooth Einstein limit on the same smooth type and applies Catino–Dameno’s rigidity theorem there. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn693533097view3"}}

**The physical shell.** Corollary 10.5 shows that one point can locate both complete energy marks. On a single minimizing sequence with separated quantile radii \(a_i\ll\rho_i\ll b_i\), suppose a sufficiently wide embedded annulus at scale \(\rho_i\) has bounded distortion, vanishing full curvature energy, and the required central harmonic control. If its middle sphere comes within \(A\rho_i\) of the inner quantile center, it separates the entire inner ball from the entire median exterior, even when that exterior is disconnected. Constructing this one chart on the physical sequence is now the extraction target.

**Competitors and heights.** Proposition 8.2 removes charged standard balls using estimates confined to their collars. It gives strict same-type descent when the removed charge exceeds the collar surcharge plus the minimizing excess, with the path remaining subcritical. On the immersed route, the manuscript recognizes specific one-sided and mixed surgery diagrams. A [global example on standard \(S^4\)](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/notes/E49_TWO_BIRTH_HEIGHT.md) follows one actual vertical height to its two zero-framed attaching circles and checks each outgoing cancellation.

**The remaining obstruction is coverage.** Positive subcritical entry on arbitrary smooth types remains open. The immersed height count does not yet select a recognized diagram on every candidate. Intrinsically, a sequence can still lack the required chart or strict competitor, converge to a closed metric outside the rigidity criterion, or admit a round restart with zero gain. The [continuation note](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/continuation-notes/AFTER_MARKED_EXTERIORS_20261125.md) prioritizes extraction of the single anchored annulus.

The PDF references resolved and repository checks passed. The proofs received bounded analytical checks. The current chat had no authenticated transcript source for archival.

Please write draft manuscripts for the different sub-investigations to be used as well, to be used for intermediate results. I want to make sure that all of the results included in the master manuscript create the fastest route to a proof, so it is better to have working drafts for the sub-investigations. Focus on analytical or theoretical results, leaving any numerics or test cases for supporting evidence. Please develop the ideas systematically, and methodically derive all of the relevant results, maximizing the coherence of the development of ideas, and the elegance of the results. At the end, describe the outstanding challenges.

I’ll check which branches already have manuscripts, then build each working draft around its own mathematical question. I’ll also review which proofs belong in those drafts and which implications the master needs to keep.

The existing neck draft already proves the buffered cap estimates, so the master can use the shorter cut argument without repeating that proof. I’m also moving the full joint volume-and-energy selection argument into the descent paper, where it sits next to the repair inequality it is meant to support.

The four specialist drafts and the immersion overview are written. The master has gone from 39 pages to 27. An independent check also sharpened the disk-repair statement: one actual repaired metric may meet \(4\pi^2\) at equality, while a limiting bound must be strict if the infimum could be unattained. I’m checking the final PDFs and references now.

The four sub-investigations now have working manuscripts. I also wrote a companion paper on the immersion estimates shared by the two extrinsic branches. One distinction sharpened the master proof. **At a finite stage, one admissible repaired metric with \(E_+\le 4\pi^2\) recognizes the smooth type.** For a minimizing sequence, a residual-energy estimate must force \(I^+(M)<4\pi^2\) to draw that conclusion from the infimum alone. Equality can remain unattained.

Each draft ends with its outstanding geometric questions. The common obstruction is coverage: producing qualifying data on every remaining smooth type. On the intrinsic route, positive subcritical entry and the subsequent construction of a separating shell, strict same-type competitor, or rigidity or termination argument remain separate steps.

I’ll check where the master uses the \(4\pi^2\) threshold, make the finite-versus-limiting distinction explicit in the proof, and add guidance to the overview for deciding which results belong in the master.

The distinction also sharpens the finite cut proof. Once the capped metrics are known to have positive Yamabe sign, their total chiral energy may equal \(8\pi^2\): at most one cap can exceed \(4\pi^2\), and a cap exactly at \(4\pi^2\) is recognized. The separate argument that proves positivity along a metric path still uses a strict bound.

Updated the [master proof](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/output/pdf/master/chiral_weyl_energy_and_smooth_poincare.pdf). Equation (2.2) on page 3 makes the distinction explicit: **one smooth positive Yamabe class with \(E_+\le4\pi^2\) recognizes the standard sphere.** For the infimum \(I^+(M)\), a strict bound below \(4\pi^2\) suffices. If \(I^+(M)=4\pi^2\) were attained, the attaining metric would recognize the sphere, whose round metric then gives \(I^+(M)=0\). Thus an estimate \(I^+(M)\le4\pi^2\) leaves precisely the unattained endpoint open.

This also sharpens Proposition 4.1. Once the capped classes are known to be positive, their combined energy may **equal \(8\pi^2\)**. At most one cap can exceed the recognition threshold, and a cap exactly at \(4\pi^2\) is standard.

The [master research overview](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/research-overview/OVERVIEW.md) now has a section titled **“What belongs in the master proof.”** Intermediate derivations stay in the sub-investigation drafts. A result enters the master when it discharges a named hypothesis, settles a previously open case, or shortens an existing argument under the same or weaker assumptions. The master gives the decisive step, cites the branch proof, and identifies what remains open.
